subject: Service-side egress binding and permitlist signoff for VPC private deployment
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@northwellhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service-side egress binding and permitlist signoff for VPC private deployment

Claire — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our security checklist, we need a short, actionable agreement on outbound connectivity from your VPC to Redwood's private-control endpoints before we flip the private deployment into prod.

Concretely, please confirm the following items so we can prepare the signed MOA and schedule the cutover: 
- Which NAT/egress path will egress traffic to our control plane: (a) centralized NAT gateway with static egress IPs, (b) dedicated egress NAT per subnet, or (c) proxy appliance (hostname/IP) managed by Northwell?
- Any inline TLS inspection or mTLS termination in the path? (note: we cannot accept TLS interception by third parties for control-plane traffic)
- DNS resolution: do you use DNS forwarders or split-horizon? Will our helper domains be resolvable from the VPC?
- Rotation cadence for ephemeral IPs (if you plan to use ephemeral NAT) and a window for planned rotations (we need a maintenance window to update permitlist entries).

We've attached a permitlist CSV template and a small diagram that shows two acceptable patterns: static egress IPs assigned to a VPC NAT, or a single customer-managed proxy with certificate pinning to Redwood's control-plane cert. If you prefer proxying, we require TLS passthrough to our endpoint (no interception) and mutual TLS from the proxy to our control-plane endpoint.

If you can reply with the selected pattern + the initial egress IPs (or proxy FQDN) by end of day Wednesday, we will draft the MOA and provide a DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: permitlist_20260830.csv (CSV list stub), egress-arch-vpc-sidecar.png (diagram stub)

From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@northwellhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Northwell Infra Ops <infra.ops@northwellhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service-side egress binding and permitlist signoff for VPC private deployment

Sergio — thanks for the clear checklist. Quick answers inline: 
- Egress path: we'll use a centralized NAT gateway in the VPC and announce a pair of static egress IPs from the gateway.
- TLS inspection: not in our path for this traffic. We'll configure the NAT to preserve TCP/TLS passthrough.
- DNS: we operate a split-horizon DNS. We will add resolution for the helper domains in the private view.
- Rotation cadence: IPs are static for the next 12 months; if rotation is needed we'll schedule a 2-hour maintenance window with 48 hrs notice.

I'll attach an initial permitlist — internal infra is preparing the CSV and the network team will confirm the final /32s by EOD Wednesday. Happy to run a quick call if you want to confirm the cert pinning/mTLS handshake details.

Claire
Sr. Cloud Engineer — Northwell Health
claire.zhou@northwellhealth.com

Subject: Re: Service-side egress binding and permitlist signoff for VPC private deployment

Claire — appreciate the quick reply and helpful answers. A couple of operational notes from my side: 
- We'll test connectivity to the static pair of egress IPs you provided via a healthcheck endpoint. Please expect outbound attempts from our diagnostic agents from the control-plane IP range; we will provide those beforehand.
- If you prefer cert pinning on your proxy, the cert fingerprint we expect is SHA256:3a:7f:... (I can paste the full fingerprint in the MOA draft).
- For DNS, confirm the FQDNs: control.redwood.control, auth.redwood.control and metrics.redwood.control. If split-horizon prevents the public view, please add them to the private view to point at our control-plane VIPs.

I'll attach a sample MOA and the smaller signoff checklist; Soojin/Neha — can you review the sample and confirm we can offer DocuSign by EOD?

Thanks,
Jordan
Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Subject: Signed MOA + final permitlist request

Claire — thanks for confirming the egress model. I've attached a prefilled MOA (signoff-moa-template.pdf) and an updated permitlist template. Two quick asks before we send the DocuSign: 
1) Please confirm the exact /32s for the two static egress IPs (we need them in CIDR form).
2) Confirm the authorized contact for notices of IP rotation and the contact for emergency firewall exceptions (name, email, and phone).

Once we receive the /32s and contact details we'll push the DocuSign request and schedule a brief smoke test (15 minutes) during the 2-hour window you mentioned.

Soojin Lee
Security Operations — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
